As trendy restaurants, bars and boutiques popped up in Nolita’s winding streets, the area started developing a separate identity from the surrounding neighborhoods. Similar to SoHo, Nolita is known for its architecture and “hip” reputation. However, Nolita lacks the high density of tourists that flock to its neighbors, allowing for a more local feel. This is an automated posting."},{"_id":"187294739","date":"2017-08-26T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"11695887","reviewer_id":"42157203","reviewer_name":"Christopher","comments":"Overall, Jennifer was a good host.  She responded to everything and does actually live close by (a good thing too, because the door code wasn't working when we arrived, but it was quickly addressed).  She was also helpful in giving us a bit of extra time for check-out.\n\nJust to say a couple things about the actual condo, the pictures do portray it in the best possible light.  Nothing deceptive, but there are elements that could use updating that are not shown.  The bathrooms need some TLC and there are lots of wires and cords everywhere (especially the bedrooms).  Everything else was clean and safe.  The kitchen is up-to-date with every appliance you should need, including a blender and toaster.  There is a newer washer and dryer right in the unit, which is very convenient.  We didn't use the TVs, but there are 3 of them - one in the main living room and one in each bedroom.  Parking was very convenient - a reserved spot that's just steps away from the ground level entrance (the condo is on the ground level and doesn't have any stairs).  There are several beach accessories waiting as well - a cooler, beach chairs and boogie boards are there for your use, along with plenty of beach towels.  There are 3 AC units and all of them worked, but they are noisy.\n\nThe noise level outside was generally good.  There were a few inconsiderate very early morning departures from other units, but nothing major.  The park across the road closes at 8pm, so there was no late-night noise to speak of.\n\nThe location in general is great.  The park across the road is not a swimming beach (no sand, too many rocks), but it's very popular for surfing and paddleboarding lessons.  There are several sandy beaches just a short drive (or healthy walk) away.  Kihei in general is a great spot to stay, as it's near several  great beaches (Big Beach in Makena is epic) and is central to a lot of things you'll want to see - the upscale Wailea area is just a short drive away and several other destinations are easily driveable from Kihei.  There are lots of food choices close by and many of them offer some of the best value you'll find in Maui.  There's also 2 supermarkets right down the road (and Foodland is open until 1am).\n\nTo summarize, the condo was more \"rustic\" than we were expecting, but I will say that in the area, you'd likely have to pay a bit more for something more updated that has 2 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms."},{"_id":"194080594","date":"2017-09-15T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"11695887","reviewer_id":"24734634","reviewer_name":"International Theatrical","comments":"Wonderful host great location"},{"_id":"202548198","date":"2017-10-11T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"11695887","reviewer_id":"78286024","reviewer_name":"Michael","comments":"Jennifer's place has everything you need in the perfect location. Haleakala or the Road to Hana. Safeway is a short ~5 min. drive & Costco & the airport are a ~30 minute drive away. Her place has everything you need: kitchen, washer/dryer, beach towels/chairs, nice outdoor patio with a nice, small pool. I highly recommend her place if you want a quiet, quaint, peaceful place to relax where everything you need is a short distance away. "},{"_id":"135193609","date":"2017-03-03T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"13299549","reviewer_id":"98885016","reviewer_name":"Benjamin","comments":"PLEASE READ. YOU'LL BE GLAD. I'm not usually one to write a review. However, I feel that strongly about my stay at this apartment that I feel I must so other travellers do not experience the problems I had. There is exstensive work happening on the corner of George Street & Bridge Street due to the construction of the light rail system(it was very disappointing that this was not mentioned anywhere in the description or throughout the booking process). On the second night 3 of the 4 guests were unable to sleep due to the excessive noise. When I rang the property manager(Arnold) to inform him of the noise and that we were unhappy about it he said that there haven't been any complaints from previous guests and that there was nothing he could do. I explained that I wasn't concerned about other guests, just my party. After much discussion his resolution was a refund for our unused nights in the apartment..............but we would have to find alternative accommodation ourselves! Not only were we wasting our vacation time trying to rectify the situation, but we then had to use more of our time trying to find alternative accommodation. With our vacation time in Sydney being only 5 nights, you can imagine how frustrating this was. Due to the short period we decided to stay on at the apartment. However, the following night there was noise outside the apartment on Bridge Street due to what looked like industrial electricians laying cables underground. Once again waking the party. The apartment itself was very disappointing, dark & outdated. You can not open the living room blinds as there is an office block a few metres directly adjacent. The bathroom is small & the overall cleanliness of the apartment was very poor. There were clumps of dust in the bathroom & when my partner moved the bed to plug in her phone charger, the dust & dirt was discusting! I found this very strange as a $243 \"cleaning fee\" is charged at the time of booking? This was relayed back to Arnold who said that he would get the cleaners back that day. Although the cleaners had returned back there, it was quite evident that they had just done the bare minimum & the large clumps of dust were still in the corner of the bathroom. By this stage of the vacation we had gone past caring and just wanted to enjoy our time in Sydney. Arnold did refund the $243 \"cleaning fee\", but only after a heated discussion. He also had to send in an electrician to fix a power point that was hanging off the wall and on a seperate occasion an electrician to change the light bulbs. Being a property management company you would think the apartment would be checked and this would of been done prior to guests entering the property? In all fairness to Arnold he was very prompt in resolving the issues, but unfortunately it was too little..."},{"_id":"138839670","date":"2017-03-21T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"13299549","reviewer_id":"96010071","reviewer_name":"Marie-Eve","comments":"Localisation exceptionnelle, parfait pour famille avec deux enfants, seul bémol, bruyant la nuit car travaux sur rue adjacente. "},{"_id":"125795493","date":"2017-01-07T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"14152437","reviewer_id":"73020984","reviewer_name":"Erik","comments":"We reserved a 4-night stay at the place, but were only allowed to stay for two. The house is advertised as being in bug-friendly Maui, so I expected some bugs. We have them where we live and most everyone does, so no big deal, right? However, when we first arrived we immediately noticed a bunch of wasps in the house. Bug-friendly to me means you’ll probably see some mosquitoes, roaches, or ants, not an infestation of wasps (I estimated close to 40 flying, on walls, or crawling on the floors during our stay). My kids were kids, and having fun counting them. The majority of the wasps were in the upstairs bedroom that we intended to use for our two little kids. We called the host and she sent her husband to vacuum up the wasps. That's all he did. He basically told us it’s to be expected and gave us no apology. He left and we inspected and immediately saw more. Over the next day we complained to her again, and finally to Airbnb. The company agreed that the place was unsuitable and immediately refunded our cleaning fee after seeing pictures of the place. The host responded by booting us out of the rental two days in. We were polite and tried to fix things in a civil manner (the main complaint was really just the wasp infestation), and we didn’t complain about anything else. We weren't prissy babies and don't really care about minor problems. But wasps flying around the rental and in your kids' room can cause some concern. Apparently, the host didn't like our complaint and saw fit to have us vacate and find lodging elsewhere for the next few nights. Imagine staying in a hotel, for example, complaining about a bug problem and having the management kick you out instead of trying to fix the issue. Crazy, right? We agreed, however, leaving the place in good order (cleaned the dishes, took out the trash and recycling, and even folded up used blankets and such). There's no reason to return pettiness with pettiness, I suppose. After that “customer is always wrong” treatment we felt it was fine anyway. Unfortunately, the host refused to refund our remaining 2 days of unused time. We stayed 2 of the 4 days at the host's request and we still got charged for 4 days. After nearly two weeks of no effort on her part to refund us, she is just now saying that we damage her bedding but is providing no details or proof. Anyway, that’s our experience. No aloha in the land of aloha really sucks, but it happens and I can’t be too bothered by it. Here are the pros and cons of the place (fairly, I hope): Pros: *super quiet – out in the middle of the country. Middle of nowhere = nice and quiet. There are tons of big pitbulls as you ride down the 2 mile dirt road to the house, but even those guys..."},{"_id":"127623558","date":"2017-01-19T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"14152437","reviewer_id":"78953092","reviewer_name":"Nicole","comments":"This cottage was in a quiet neighborhood close to town; secluded enough to relax after a long day of adventures. For us city dwellers, staying in this cottage is like having close contact with nature while still having the convenience of a modern house. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here for a week or recommend my friends to do so."},{"_id":"147263357","date":"2017-04-25T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"14152437","reviewer_id":"51974847","reviewer_name":"Suzanne","comments":"Kandy's place outside of Paia is exactly as described, yet even so, delightfully surprised us. Every detail was charming and one could sense she had gone to a lot of effort to make her place welcoming. After spending time in other parts of Maui, it was a relief to arrive \"home\" to this seemingly secluded, lush paradise. Most of our time was spent on the deck; the wind blowing through the tropical plants, the occasional rain, all served as a soothing (and at other times exhilarating) backdrop to our activities. Then there are the animals. My children delighted in the tame free range chickens roaming about, as well as the geckos and rabbit. We were able to spend about half an hour with Kandy, who was rushing from one thing to the next, but generously took time to show us around her property and even offered us some of the ripened fruit available. We would have loved to spend more time with her, but our schedules never matched up. Perhaps next time? "},{"_id":"147831287","date":"2017-04-28T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"14152437","reviewer_id":"126362459","reviewer_name":"Jeremy","comments":"This place was an awesome find. There are a lot of great restaurants nearby, and we had an awesome meal our first night thanks to the list of suggestions Clark left in the apartment! We had a small hiccup at check-in, but it was resolved within a few minutes, and we were able to get our keys. The apartment was spacious, clean, and had everything we needed. Most importantly, we felt very safe there and walking in the area. The only things to be aware of - the two flights of stairs up to the apartment are a little slanted and feel a bit like a fun house, so keep that in mind if you have issues with stairs. There are also very hot pipes running in the apartment that don't have any warning stickers, so they could easily burn a child or someone that might accidentally touch them. Not really a negative, just something to keep in mind if you're traveling with little ones! The location is in a friendly neighbourhood and the houses are very close together. I can well understand why it would not be suitable for parties or large get-togethers.  The house has a big, comfortable porch, surrounded by palm trees where we sat most of the time during our stay.\n\nThe kitchen and bathrooms had all the necessities required, as well as enough beach towels, bath towels, and the laundry facilities had a modern washer and dryer. The garage was great too, as we had rented a fairly big jeep and there was plenty of room and was really spacious. \n\nWe never had the chance to meet Nina in person, but our written communication was excellent. Her response was quick and reliable. \n\nIf I had to give a constructive criticism, it would be 2 small issues.  One, because we always returned back to the house at night, we had to always turn on our flashlight in order to lead us safely up the path to the stairs where the main entrance was located. Perhaps one more motion detector light would be nice. Secondly, we were too incompetent to use the television, meaning not user-friendly.  Although Nina left instructions, we weren't able to watch it, which DID NOT matter to us and didn't warrant a call.\n\nI would recommend Nina''s place for a nice quiet, stay in the North Shore area."},{"_id":"126424460","date":"2017-01-11T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"15167619","reviewer_id":"13623630","reviewer_name":"Trisha","comments":"We had such a great stay at Nina's place. She was very communicative and helpful from before our stay and throughout. Check in and checkout were also easy and seamless. \n\nIt was perfectly spacious for two couples, and we had all the tools we needed to make our own meals. You will want to eat out too--so many great places to eat on the island! The house is such a short walk to the beach, we caught plenty of sunrises and sunsets with little effort. We also got to see lots of marine life, including huge turtles, without having to pay for resort snorkeling!\n\nYou won't regret staying here if you want a relaxing experience away from the hustle and bustle of Waikiki but close to some great beaches. I'd you rent a car, you can always drive to the other beaches and party's if the island, but retreat to north shore when you're ready to kick back. We'd stay here again without hesitation!"},{"_id":"128319231","date":"2017-01-23T05:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"15167619","reviewer_id":"98924814","reviewer_name":"Wilton","comments":"I had a great time staying at Nina's place on the North shore of Oahu. If you'd like to do some shopping, there's a strip of shops and restaurants about 10 minutes away from Nina's place by car with boutiques, surf shops, and cafes, as well as many other types of shops.  And there is also a great farmers market that is close by that you have to check out if you stay here. There isn't an air conditioning unit, but given the time of year that we visited (March/April), it wasn't an issue at all. The house is in the perfect location, a 2 minute walk to a beautiful beach and a 6 minute drive to Haleiwa that has shops, restaurants & grocery stores. \nThe home was airy and spacious, with 2 bedrooms & 2 bathrooms with 2 showers, it was amazing! Nina was a wonderful host and was so easy to get in touch with, and left coffee & chocolates for our arrival, so nice. The house is also well equipped with all of the little things you might want, like beach towels, shampoo & conditioner, salt and pepper, dish soap, toilet paper and even board games. It feels like being at home.\nThe deck is the perfect spacious spot to hang out, and all of the furniture is clean & comfy. The entire house was clean and welcoming. There are great ceiling fans in every room and there are windows with screens you can open so you always have a great breeze through the house. The kitchen is well stocked with all of the necessities, and is a bright happy space to have breakfast. \nThe outdoor shower was really nice, it is huge and airy and perfect when coming back from the beach to get the sand off. The entire yard is really big too, and there is a big picnic table if you want to eat outdoors. The neighbourhood is really friendly & quiet (the evenings are super quiet, you can even hear the ocean from the front deck!) and super safe. \nI highly recommend this house - It was the perfect spot for our getaway and we truly felt at home at Nina's. "},{"_id":"147798748","date":"2017-04-28T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"15167619","reviewer_id":"121091882","reviewer_name":"Keith","comments":"This was a great place for my colleague and I to stay while visiting Oahu for work at Schofield Barracks. "},{"_id":"160602617","date":"2017-06-14T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"15167619","reviewer_id":"101251934","reviewer_name":"Ben","comments":"Palm Tree House is on beautiful grounds about 1.5 blocks from the beach.  We could not see or hear the ocean from this home but we did hear beautiful birds each morning.  The bedrooms are clean and comfortable.  The bathrooms are both located in the hall and do not join to any bedrooms.  This made it quite awkward for sharing space with the couple we traveled with.  One shower is its own room.  You have to change your clothes directly in the shower.  The toilet is in a room separate from this shower.  We were able to work it out, but it was rather uncomfortable.\nWe loved the lanai and the beautiful, well manicured grounds. The air around Palm Tree House smells like flowers.  Nina was very helpful.  We had a difficult time cooling the place down when we first arrived, but she patiently explained the ceiling fans (there is no a/c).  When there were cross-breezes it was quite comfortable.  \nWe appreciated being able to use the body boards and beach chairs.  We found the best waves near Laie (North Shore)  The waves at the beach near Palm Tree House were very gentle and relaxing. We were told that the waves were in \"hibernation\" during our trip in early June (I'm not sure if this is a common thing or not.)\nOur favorite places on North Shore were Haleiwa (kayaking, shaved ice, food trucks, cute shops, Ted's Pies at the grocery store), Polynesian Cultural Center (the best experience/show of the entire trip),  and Hukilau Beach (awesome waves!).  \nOverall, Palm Tree House is a great place for relaxing at the end of an exciting day.  Thank you Nina!"},{"_id":"168983511","date":"2017-07-11T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"15167619","reviewer_id":"111751564","reviewer_name":"Jawalkerpe","comments":"Nice place a little warm in July"},{"_id":"177147193","date":"2017-08-01T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"15167619","reviewer_id":"129691724","reviewer_name":"Chris","comments":"The house is very clean, well equipped and in a great location. The location provides a getaway from the extremely busy/touristy area of Waikiki as well as close proximity to the beautiful north shore. We stayed at Nina’s place for two weeks and didn’t want to leave!  We loved escaping back to the North Shore after fighting traffic and crowds on soccer days.  Other days we hiked Manoa Falls, Koko Crater Railway and Ka’ena point, went paddle boarding and jumping off the bridge in Haleiwa and snorkeling at Sharks Cove and our nearby beach.  We also spent a day at Waikiki beach and Pearl Harbor.  We stopped twice at the Dole plantation for delicious dole whip and explored the shops and farmer’s market in Wailua, be sure to check out the laid back coffee and chocolate tour at the local roasting company. Most days we walked around the block to the beach to watch the sunset and watch the turtles feed along the shore.\nThe World Cup started during our trip and we were able to record all the games we wanted on the DVR and watch them during breakfast, that made us very happy!\nThank you Nina for such a welcoming and wonderful stay, it is a trip we will never forget!"},{"_id":"292767546","date":"2018-07-18T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"15167619","reviewer_id":"268985","reviewer_name":"Pippi -","comments":"This house is lovely and Nina is truly a fantastic host. The only drawback, and this is of no fault of the host and I doubt she could do anything about it, but the neighbor's dogs (across the street) bark incessantly at times which was a bit maddening.  But I had to spend a lot of time working remotely each day and most guests probably won't spend that much time in the house so hopefully it won't be an issue.   This is a great place and I would certainly recommend it to anyone wanting to stay in a Waialua. We are a block from the Apollo, a music hall which is credited with launching the careers of some of the most talented African American artists since the 1930s. The amateur night every Wednesday is still incredibly competitive and definitely a fun thing to do in the city. There are several great jazz bars within a five minute walk, and the Studio Museum (a two-minute walk) is an excellent museum dedicated to showcasing African American art. (The gift shop is also highly recommended.) We are one block away from 125th street--the main thoroughfare in Harlem filled with lots of shopping (and some of the best outlet shopping in Manhattan), and there are several neighborhood walking tours that leave just minutes from our apartment organized around a variety of subjects, including food, heritage, jazz, and gospel-themed tours. There were plenty of fresh clean towels in the bathroom, and just enough in the kitchen - tea, some drinks in the fridge, etc. - to make me feel at home. The only thing that was a little tricky was the wifi, which works a bit differently from some hotels, in that you have to unplug it so it doesn't overheat and then make sure it's plugged back in so it doesn't lose power. My devices didn't seem to be able to quite stay connected consistently and my iPad never connected at all, but Alina mentioned she'd never had that issue before, so it might have just been my iPad! She was very sweet and offered to bring her laptop by so I could get online without interruption, but I was able to manage for the most part! I would recommend Alina as a host and I would be glad to stay in her place again. He responded quickly to all of our questions, requests, and concerns. On numerous occasions I texted him and he responded within minutes. In regards to the flat, there were definitely pros and cons. Pros: great view, elevator, air conditioning, full size fridge and fully stocked kitchen ideal for eating in. Cons: The flat is not great for tall people... the kitchen and back bedroom both have fairly low sloped ceilings. The hot water was unpredictable but I didn't bring this to Ati's attention so I'm sure he would fix it. There was a strong chemical odor almost like a hair salon that seemed to come and go. Also there seemed to be a mold/mildew problem in the bathroom. I know this is common in old buildings but with the humidity it was particularly bothersome. Overall I had a great time staying here. In my experience with Istanbul flats this was a normal experience. I would also mention that the flat is smaller than the photos make it look. Luckily the balcony is nice ;) In regards to the neighborhood, it's a fantastic location especially if you plan on doing touristy stuff but want to also be close to Taksim. It's a 5 minute walk uphill to Taksim and a 10 minute walk downhill to get the Tram which can take you to all of the sites like Sultan Ahmet, Top Kapi, and the Bazaars. You can also easily walk to the Kabatas ferry station. I felt totally safe in the neighborhood. There is a lot of construction so it's not the most beautiful street in the city but it's convenience makes it worth it. Overall I would recommend this flat. Like I said, any problems that were brought to Ati's attention were dealt with promptly so that was great. Thanks so much!"},{"_id":"19331811","date":"2014-09-10T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"3640004","reviewer_id":"919918","reviewer_name":"Daniel","comments":"The flat  is nice located with a beautiful view to the Bosporus/ sea of marmara. A bus goes straight from the airport to Taksim Sqaure and the apartment is a couple of blocks from Taksim square and only a tad furthur in the opposite direction to the T1 tram that is easy to maneuver. It connects New Town to Old Town and makes it really easy (and cheap!) to get around. The place also has a fantastic balcony with a lovely view. While Ati was a responsive communicator, we did have an issue with meeting up to get the house keys. Something came up and he was unable to meet the first person in our party to arrive. This made it very difficult to access the apartment since she told him that her phone would not work in Istanbul beforehand. The neighbors who had the keys didn't seem well informed that we were coming and there is a trick to opening the door that is not very intuitive. After a long day of traveling, it is notable that this process could have been much smoother. The only other issue that we had was with the hot water. During our stay, the hot water was very unreliable and alternated between ice cold and scalding hot, when it worked at all. Ati was responsive, came to take a look, but couldn't seem to get repairmen out to fix the problem(it seems the hot water heater failed). The water problem was a bit out of Ati's control. He was very apologetic about the meet up. He bought us a beer, stayed in contact and let us leave our bags past check out time on the day we had to leave since we had a late flight. He also suggested a great place for us to eat. Other than the 2 issues, we had a lovely stay and found the apartment to be a perfect fit for the three of us! The balcony is lovely to sit in and enjoy a meal or some drinks in the evening with a nice view of the sea. The bathroom shower cabinet is broken and doesn't shut - hope Ati fixes this soon ! Some reviewers have complained about the wifi but Ati had sent me the passwords beforehand and it worked well. Communication with Ati was a bit slow but didn't pose much of a problem. There is a steep hill to reach the apartment (as in most of Istanbul) but this can be easily avoided by taking two sets of stairs which was a great relief ! It took barely 7 mins to walk to Taksim square (which has a lot of shops/cafes/bars/restaurants and the metro) and has a few mini supermarkets 2-3 mins away which have all the essentials. The only thing that wasn't that easy was that we were reaching the airport at 9am but the apartment was only ready at 2pm as Ati had guests before. He did allow us to come in and leave our bags and take the keys at 1pm while the cleaning lady was there which was very helpful but I wish I had known this before making the booking as I may have tried booking a place with an earlier check in time. As the time is not on the description page - I suggest you check with Ati what time you can check in before booking if you are planning to come in early ! Thanks, Lauren and Vince!"},{"_id":"14089745","date":"2014-06-11T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"602888","reviewer_id":"14377191","reviewer_name":"Deb And Thom","comments":"This was our first-ever AirBNB experience, and it was wonderful.\r\n\r\nAs the date of our reservation approached, Lauren kept in contact with us.  And on the day of our trip, I was able to text both her and her brother, who was going to meet us with the key, updates.  They responded promptly back.\r\n\r\nWe were met in front of the building shortly after we arrived and we were very grateful for the help with our luggage and the working elevator.  (We had forgotten how narrow hallways are in Manhattan apartment buildings.)\r\n\r\nThe apartment gets a good deal of sunlight, which we enjoyed, though you can put down the shades for privacy.  It has everything we needed and lots of things (like the TV) which we never used.  The shower had hot water, the Air Conditioners blew out cold air, and the bed had fresh sheets and was comfortable.  We have both lived in NYC, so we knew that apartments are narrow and storage space is at a premium, therefore, we knew what to expect.  They have done a great job of trying to make as much free space as they can in their apartment, and that was very much appreciated.  They also cleaned out a drawer in the dresser for us and left us a bag of mini-muffins as a Welcome to NYC treat.  We instantly felt at home. \r\n\r\nAnd the neighborhood is wonderful.  Coffee, Bagels, Diners, Grocery stores and Pharmacies, and Restaurants and Bars galore,  are within a short walk of the building.  (Try the Belgian place if you are in the Neighborhood.  Say Hi to Remy for us.)  My wife found a Yoga place a couple of blocks away, and I was able to walk a little ways to Central Park and go jogging.  We were also able to rent bikes from Peddle Pushers (get helmets and a lock) and take them around the city and across into Brooklyn for the day.  Bike lanes are available on 2nd and 1st Ave.  \r\n\r\nIn conclusion, if you are considering this apartment, book it.  The pictures are accurate, the description is accurate, Lauren is pleasant and responsive, and you would be hard-pressed to find a better neighborhood in the city.  We had a fantastic stay and would recommend this place to family and friends.  Not to mention, we would gladly stay again.\r\n\r\nTips:  \r\n\r\nDon't put stuff on the stove, the pilot lights are always on and the top of the stove stays hot.\r\n\r\nShut the door to the office to keep the bedroom cool at night.\r\n\r\nThe shower pressure can take off skin.  I'm not complaining, but be careful.\r\n\r\nThere is no coffee maker, but there is a Dunkin Donuts around the corner, so I was pleased I didn't have to make my own. (There is an espresso machine but it frightened me.)"},{"_id":"14635645","date":"2014-06-23T04:00:00.000Z","listing_id":"602888","reviewer_id":"4411368","reviewer_name":"William","comments":"Lauren and Vincent are a super nice couple.
